Order the clusters of an alluvial to reduce crossing flows

Source: R/minimize_crossing_alluvial.R
minimize_crossing_alluvial.Rd

In an alluvial plot, flows between clusters drawn far apart cross many other flows and make the plot unreadable. minimize_crossing_alluvial() computes an order of the clusters that places clusters exchanging many nodes next to each other. It is a heuristic, not an optimal solution to the crossing problem.

The function builds a network of clusters: two clusters are tied when nodes move from one to the other between windows, with a cosine weight \(n_{ab} / \sqrt{\bar{s}_a \bar{s}_b}\), \(n_{ab}\) being the number of moving nodes and \(\bar{s}_a\) the mean size of cluster \(a\) over its windows. It then removes the ties one by one, from the weakest to the strongest, and records at each step the connected component of each cluster. Clusters are ordered by this sequence of components: clusters that stay together until the strongest ties are removed end up side by side.

Usage

minimize_crossing_alluvial(
  alluv_dt,
  intertemporal_cluster_column = NULL,
  node_id = NULL,
  window_column = "window"
)

Arguments

alluv_dt

A data frame created with networks_to_alluv().

intertemporal_cluster_column

Character scalar, the column with the dynamic clusters.

node_id

Character scalar, the column with the node identifiers.

window_column

Character scalar, the column with the time windows ("window" by default).

Value

alluv_dt with a new column minimize_crossing_order, the rank of each cluster, that plot_alluvial() uses to order the blocks.

Details

The alluvial method (following clusters over time with networks_to_alluv(), minimize_crossing_alluvial() and plot_alluvial()) was initiated by Alexandre Truc.

Examples

networks <- build_dynamic_networks(
  nodes = subset(Nodes_stagflation, source_type == "Stagflation"),
  directed_edges = Ref_stagflation,
  source_id = "source_id",
  target_id = "target_id",
  time_variable = "source_year",
  time_window = 10,
  cooccurrence_method = "coupling_similarity",
  edges_threshold = 1,
  verbose = FALSE
)
#> Warning: The last window is shorter than the others.
#> ℹ The data end in 2013, but the last window ends in 2014.
networks <- add_clusters(
  networks,
  clustering_method = "leiden",
  objective_function = "modularity",
  seed = 123,
  verbose = FALSE
)
networks <- merge_dynamic_clusters(
  networks,
  cluster_id = "cluster_leiden",
  node_id = "source_id",
  threshold_similarity = 0.51,
  similarity_type = "partial"
)
#> Warning: 3 pairs of consecutive windows share no node: their clusters cannot be matched.
#> ℹ Clusters are matched through the nodes they share. In a network of documents
#>   (coupling), each node has one date: use sliding windows (`overlapping_window
#>   = TRUE` in `build_dynamic_networks()`). If windows already slide, the nodes
#>   may have changed completely, or the threshold may leave a window without
#>   edges.
alluv_dt <- networks_to_alluv(
  networks,
  intertemporal_cluster_column = "dynamic_cluster_leiden",
  node_id = "source_id"
)
#> ℹ No color column in the graphs: no colour kept (see `color_alluvial()`).
#> ℹ No cluster_label column in the graphs: no label kept (see `name_clusters()`).

alluv_dt <- minimize_crossing_alluvial(
  alluv_dt,
  intertemporal_cluster_column = "dynamic_cluster_leiden",
  node_id = "source_id"
)
#> Warning: no non-missing arguments to max; returning -Inf
unique(alluv_dt[, c("dynamic_cluster_leiden", "minimize_crossing_order")])
#> Key: <dynamic_cluster_leiden>
#>     dynamic_cluster_leiden minimize_crossing_order
#>                     <char>                   <int>
#>  1:                   cl_1                       1
#>  2:                  cl_10                      12
#>  3:                  cl_11                       3
#>  4:                  cl_12                       4
#>  5:                  cl_13                       5
#>  6:                   cl_2                       6
#>  7:                   cl_3                       7
#>  8:                   cl_4                       8
#>  9:                   cl_5                       9
#> 10:                   cl_6                      10
#> 11:                   cl_7                      11
#> 12:                   cl_8                      13
#> 13:                   cl_9                       2
